svg.title: A cost-push (supply) shock: inflation up, output gap down
svg.desc: Three panels over 16 quarters after a cost-push shock that adds 1 percentage point a year to the Phillips curve, for the rule with phi_pi = 1.5 and with phi_pi = 3. On impact inflation is 1.283 vs 0.839 and the gap -0.513 vs -0.839. Educational demos made to show an open-source tool. Not research.

g.text: A cost-push (supply) shock: inflation up, output gap down

text.style: fill: #57606a; font: 11px 'DejaVu Sans', 'Bitstream Vera Sans', 'Computer Modern Sans Serif', 'Lucida Grande', 'Verdana', 'Geneva', 'Lucid', 'Arial', 'Helvetica', 'Avant Garde', sans-serif; text-anchor: start

g.text: Three-equation New Keynesian model, quarterly, calibration as in Galí (2015), ch. 3. Pure simulation, no data.

text.style: fill: #57606a; font: 9.5px 'DejaVu Sans', 'Bitstream Vera Sans', 'Computer Modern Sans Serif', 'Lucida Grande', 'Verdana', 'Geneva', 'Lucid', 'Arial', 'Helvetica', 'Avant Garde', sans-serif; text-anchor: start

g.text: Educational demos made to show an open-source tool. Not research. Woodford (2003); Clarida, Galí and Gertler (1999); Galí (2015).

g.text: Same shock, two rules. Shock persistence 0.5.
